clarified_description: A `breaking` boolean flag is added to the shared changelog entry shape used by both `pixie-sandbox/pixie-sandbox-site` and `pixie-sandbox/sandbox-changelog-api`, meaning the same thing in each repository. In the data files the field is optional and omitted when false, so the four existing entries in each repository need no change and continue to render as non-breaking. On the site, a marked entry renders a small `Breaking` pill next to its title on the changelog page, styled in an amber warning colour that stands out from the muted date and reading-time styling, and carrying the accessible text `Breaking change:` in DOM order before the entry heading so a screen reader announces it before the title. In the RSS feed at `/changelog.xml`, each marked entry's `<title>` is prefixed with `[Breaking] ` and its `<item>` gains a `<category>breaking</category>` element; non-breaking entries are unchanged. The changelog API returns `breaking: boolean` on every entry (defaulted to `false` where the source omits the field, so consumers see a consistent shape), accepts `?breaking=true` to return only breaking entries, and responds `400 Bad Request` if the `breaking` query parameter is present with any other value.

constraints.detail: The `breaking` field must have identical semantics in `pixie-sandbox/pixie-sandbox-site` and `pixie-sandbox/sandbox-changelog-api`: same field name, boolean type, `false` when omitted from source, no coercion of other truthy/falsy values. There is no shared types package or runtime enforcement — parity is by convention across the two PRs.

The API change is additive and backward compatible: existing consumers see the same response with one extra optional-shaped field they can ignore, and the `?breaking=true` filter is opt-in. No version bump, no deprecation window.

The API must reject any `breaking` query value other than the literal string `true` with `400`, not silently coerce (e.g. treat `1`, `yes`, or an empty value as true). This keeps the parameter's meaning single-valued and avoids consumers relying on undocumented coercion.

The Breaking pill must be accessible: the accessible text `Breaking change:` must be in the DOM in reading order before the entry heading (not injected via CSS `content`, not `aria-hidden`, not placed after the title with `aria-label` reordering).

RSS 2.0 has no standard element for breaking-change markers. This spec chooses `<category>breaking</category>` (a standard RSS element with a fixed literal value) plus a `[Breaking] ` prefix on `<title>`, so a feed reader sees the marker in the visible title even if it ignores `<category>`.

contracts.definition: GET on the changelog list endpoint served by `handle()` in `sandbox-changelog-api`. Response entries gain a new required field `breaking: boolean` (always present, `false` where source omits it). Query parameters: `breaking` is optional; when present, its only accepted value is the exact string `true`, which filters the response to entries with `breaking === true`. Any other value → HTTP 400. Absence of the parameter → response contains all entries. The response envelope (array or object wrapper) is otherwise unchanged.

GET `/changelog.xml` on `pixie-sandbox-site`. RSS 2.0 output structure unchanged except: for each `<item>` whose underlying entry has `breaking === true`, the `<title>` text is prefixed with `[Breaking] ` (bracketed literal, single trailing space, applied after XML escaping) and the `<item>` contains an additional `<category>breaking</category>` child element.

flows.title: API request handling for the breaking filter

must: The system shall carry a `breaking` boolean on each changelog entry with the same meaning in the site and in the API.
The system shall treat a source-data entry without a `breaking` field as `breaking: false`, so the four existing entries in each repository remain non-breaking without modification.
WHERE a changelog entry has `breaking: true`, the site shall render a visible `Breaking` pill next to the entry title on the changelog page.
WHERE a changelog entry has `breaking: true`, the site shall place the accessible text `Breaking change:` in DOM order before the entry title so a screen reader announces it before the title.
WHERE the Breaking pill is shown, the system shall meet WCAG 2.1 AA contrast in both light and dark themes.

WHERE a changelog entry has `breaking: true`, the RSS feed shall prefix the corresponding `<item>` `<title>` with the literal `[Breaking] ` (bracketed word, single trailing space) and shall emit a `<category>breaking</category>` element inside that `<item>`.
WHERE a changelog entry does not have `breaking: true`, the RSS feed shall render its `<item>` with no `[Breaking] ` prefix and no `<category>breaking</category>` element.
The changelog API shall return `breaking` as a boolean on every entry in every list response, using `false` for entries whose source data omits the field.
WHEN a client calls the changelog API with `?breaking=true`, the system shall return only entries whose `breaking` is `true`.
IF the changelog API receives the query parameter `breaking` with any value other than the exact string `true`, THEN the system shall respond `400 Bad Request`.
WHEN a client calls the changelog API with `?breaking=true` and no entries are marked breaking, the system shall respond `200 OK` with an empty list.

The engineer picks the entry point when writing `test/breaking.test.ts` using `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` per the repo's CLAUDE.md, testing `handle()` directly rather than opening a socket.
AC10 (`existing entries unchanged`) is a diff-review criterion, not a unit test — the reviewer verifies by inspecting the diff on both `data/changelog.json` files.
outcome: A changelog entry can be marked as breaking, and that marking travels consistently to the changelog page (a pill next to the title, announced to screen readers as `Breaking change:` before the title), the RSS feed (a `[Breaking] ` title prefix and a `<category>breaking</category>` element), and the changelog API (a `breaking` boolean on every entry, filterable with `?breaking=true`).
rationale:
**Shape over surface.** The feature description asks for one flag that means the same thing in two places. That's the load-bearing decision — everything else is how each surface expresses it. `breaking: boolean`, optional in source, always-present in API response, `false` when the source is silent.

**Optional in source, boolean in API.** The two forms serve different readers. Existing source entries stay byte-identical so the current PRs of that JSON don't churn; the API projects every entry through a `breaking: entry.breaking === true` normalisation so consumers get one shape and don't have to encode `undefined === false` themselves.

**RSS: title prefix AND category.** RSS 2.0 has no dedicated `<breaking>` element and this spec deliberately avoids a custom namespace. `<category>breaking</category>` is a standard element with a well-defined slot, and the `[Breaking] ` title prefix is what a human reading a feed reader will actually see. Both are cheap; together they cover clients that render `<category>` and clients that don't.

**Site: pill in DOM order, not aria trickery.** The `Breaking change:` accessible text sits in the DOM before the h2, so both sighted reading order and screen-reader reading order announce it first. This avoids the fragile pattern of `aria-label` reordering an element that follows the title visually.

**API: strict query parsing.** `?breaking=true` returns breaking-only; anything else 400s. The alternative (accept `false`/`1`/`yes` as coerced values) would silently expand the parameter's meaning and lock in coercion consumers might rely on. Strict is easy to relax later; loose is not easy to tighten.

**Backward compatibility.** The API change is additive: a new optional-shaped field on each entry and a new query parameter. Existing consumers ignoring the field see identical behaviour; existing consumers passing no `breaking` query see identical results. No flag, no version, no deprecation window.

**Duplicate type in the site.** The site declares `ChangelogEntryData` in `components/changelog/ChangelogEntry.tsx` and redeclares it locally in `app/changelog.xml/route.ts`. Both must gain `breaking?: boolean`. Consolidating them into a shared module is out of scope — the engineer may do it but is not required to.

Do not use truthy coercion; explicit strict equality to `true` avoids treating `1`, `"true"`, or other values as breaking if source data drifts.

The API's `breaking` query parameter is compared to the exact string `"true"`; any other value (including `"false"`, `"1"`, empty string, repeated parameter) responds `400 Bad Request`. Absence of the parameter is not an error — it returns all entries.
